_comment: Direct3D device and texture-cache records (std3D.c, 2026-11-14). Std3DDevice: the table at 0x00900b40 (0x22c bytes per driver, D3D_SelectDriver: g_pStd3D_CurDevice = &table[driverIdx]); Std3DTexture: the 0x98-byte texture record std3D_AddToTextureCache fills and D3D_LinkTexture / D3D_UnlinkTexture keep in the cache list (g_pD3dTextureList, its tail at 0x0080694c). Typing Std3DTexture.nSize as int also fixes std3D_AddToTextureCache: the original stores the size from an integer register (MOV [EDI+0x88],ECX), the generated code stored the float bits of a reused stack slot, `*(float *)(texture + 0x88) = fStack_1c` with fStack_1c = (float)(w * h), so the device's free texture memory went wrong by a float's bit pattern per texture.

structs.name: Std3DDevice
structs.comment: A Direct3D driver of the display device (0x22c bytes, the table at 0x00900b40).
fields: a hardware device: its z-buffer is created in video memory (DDSCAPS 0x4000), else in system memory (0x800)
D3D_SelectDriver creates a z-buffer only when set
8-bit paletted textures (std3D_AddToTextureCache's usePalette, the colormap path of rdCache_SendFaceListToHardware)
tested with nUnknown18 before the hardware path uses alpha (rdCache_SendFaceListToHardware)
0: D3D_SelectDriver also picks a 4-bit-alpha texture format
non-zero: textures whose width and height differ are handled apart (std3D_AddToTextureCache)
bit 0x10 selects the z-buffer mode UINT_00900534 (16 / 2)
texture memory left: D3D_LinkTexture subtracts a texture's nSize, D3D_UnlinkTexture adds it
DDBD_* the device supports (0x100 32, 0x400 16, 0x800 8 bits; D3D_CreateZBuffer)

structs.name: Std3DTexture
structs.comment: A texture in the Direct3D texture cache (0x98 bytes, std3D_AddToTextureCache).
fields: frame of the last use (D3D_EvictTexture drops the oldest)
